utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let's go now to -- we're still on 12 July but I'd like to go to a chapter. It's page 85 in the book which is 97 in e-court. And at 53110, this is something -- sorry, 53.13.0, something which is called "Luke." And can you just give us a bit of the background. What is the significance of Luke? What are we about to see very briefly?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the women and children and elderly that have been taken from Potocari on the buses and brought to Luke, and from there they're dropped off and they will walk to Kladanj, to the free territory as they refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was there any evidence in the investigation indicating any separating of men at Luke?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we know that there were men that were separated there. We have a survivor of an execution who describes being taken off a bus and later this group is executed; he, however, survives it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's start this short section.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We've now stopped at Luke now and we're at a section called Luke-Kladanj road 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how is this related to the last clip we saw where we saw people getting off?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. This is a continuation of that same footage. Now they're walking along the road towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this a location that is spoken to in the investigation, from now, of Colonel Boering?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. I didn't get to hear his testimony these last couple days, but I know in the past he's referred to Luke and Kladanj road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's play it here at 54.27.9. And this is at the book page 87 and 99 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could ... we now have -- are at 55.36.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've obviously gotten a different quality video. Can you tell us roughly what this is of, where this is roughly?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also in the same location, obviously the people have -- are still walking towards Kladanj, and in this particular scene you see Colonel Boering from UNPROFOR, from DutchBat in this shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, he is the person to the left of the screen in the camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The far left as we look at it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've stopped at 55.48.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where we are now?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there -- you're getting closer to Kladanj. You're seeing more people, and I think shortly you are going to see ABiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. There's a section of these people at the Tuzla air base which I will skip at this point and go on to 13 July in a segment that begins on page 106 in e-court and page 94 of the book. But I think it's about break time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is break time. Ms. Gallagher, would you please follow the usher. We would like to see you back in about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break and we'll resume at 25 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Could I meanwhile inquire what the plans are as far as the continuation of the testimony of this witness is concerned? Do you want to continue on Monday or ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would discuss with the Defence if they have a lengthy cross and -- because I believe this witness is fairly flexible and we do have another, as you know, Dutch officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that. But of course at the same time we don't want it to be split up into a hundred little pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could briefly deal with it at the end of today's session. Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Now, let's -- we are still with the trial video 28780. Let's go to a 13 July segment that we've -- basically is called: "Mladic in Srebrenica." It's from V0009267 from 06 to 0239.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've now stopped at 02.30.5, and for reference this is page 95 of the book which is 107 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this man in the far left whose face is partially obscured in the still, has that person been identified in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he actually identified himself. It is Petar Salapura who is chief of intelligence administration for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we've ended at 02.39.7. And I will skip some of Potocari, I think the Court has seen some of that, and I would like to go to V0009268. It is a clip that the investigation has dated 13 June 1996 and it is -- was a relatively long speech of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have skipped down to the relevant part near the end of the talk. And can you, Ms. Gallagher, just put us in a little bit of context, June 1996, where is this, and any significant individuals that are with Mladic around the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What page are we in the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's -- gets to page 174 in the book, Mr. President, which is 186 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could -- let's start with putting that up on the screen so Ms. Gallagher can put us in context, so that would be page 186 in e-court. Oh, brilliant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so could you just put this in a little context. Where is this? Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. You don't -- this is a small clip of a much longer -- of much longer original footage but he and the Main Staff -- commanders of the Main Staff have been travelling in the Zepa area and he's been pointing out some of the historical and important places during the war. And now they're having a picnic and he's -- well, he's giving a speech. And you asked about who we can also see. You see in this photo number 2, that's Colonel Beara who is chief of security for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And he's identified how? Because that's not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can certainly identify him myself. He was one of our defendants in the Popovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can all see that this is a very blurry still. Were you able to get a better look as you see the whole video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you'll see more of that side of the table and you will see -- if I can point out another photograph that you asked for other members that were there that we can also identify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I have got this down to its bare bones which I think is -- will be fine --

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- so let's just see what we can see from the video. But I think we'll all remember you mentioning when we had the document which is P01087, e-court page 23, from the Srebrenica court binder which was a map that was signed off on by General Mladic and had what you called a cross on it. And you -- we may recall that you'd said you'd seen a video about this. Is this the video we're about to see that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the video that I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that was e-court page 24, excuse me. And I think we can play this segment of the speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we start at 31.59.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. It ended 32.47.9, with the statement we see on the screen. Your Honour, with your leave I have one more chapter and I know Your Honour is very familiar with this. It's a Srebrenica-related film. We've called it the Skorpion video, and we see that it goes on for a few minutes. It would be the last video I would play today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is from V009267, roughly 010615 to 012612. We're starting at 01.07.13.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're ending at 01.26.12.6 and could we in the stills book which is 28781 go to e-court page 168.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as we're waiting for that to come up, is it true that the individuals we see shot on this video are Safet Fejzic, Sidik Salkic, Azmir Alispahic, Smajil Ibrahimovic, Dino Salihovic, and Juso Delic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I will ask others about this unit and about this location, but can you confirm that these six people were reported missing from Srebrenica, to the fall of Srebrenica, July 11th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, they were young men from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd ask for 168 to come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 168 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In e-court, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So these are the people that you've just confirmed, is that right, and this is the page and this information is correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am finished. I would like to offer 28780 into evidence and 28781 and the trial video has with it the full transcript of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, no objection to the video. My only concern is the stills book does not have B/C/S for the table of contents which I think would be the only substantive part that may not able to be followed by our client. So in that sense I would ask for it to be marked for identification until at least the table of contents is translated so that it can be followed by our client in the language he understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the table of contents is without translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have that and I have somehow misplaced in providing it to the Defence. So we will get that to them of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it will be MFI'd. First the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, first the video 28780, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Receives number P1147, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Then the book to be marked for identification, the trial video book.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28781 receives number P1148, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Mr. Ivetic, apparently the examination-in-chief has been concluded on this subject matter. How much time would you need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't anticipate needing more than 30, 40 minutes, perhaps closer to 30 than to 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Today we have ten minutes left. Mr. McCloskey, and -- could you -- would we start in finalising the cross-examination Monday or ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Our next witness is fine, I'm sure, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I say "Monday," but you should say Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course we are not sitting on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, being able to start within an hour of the scheduled time is very good. So he will be ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Ivetic, then you could start your cross-examination now and then we'll -- in ten minutes we'll adjourn and you could then continue Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Mladic Defence team. Mr. Mladic is asking for a brief consultation -- well, if it can be done quickly then--

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, I said several times. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With your leave I can begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, hello again.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to just remind you before we begin that since we're both speaking English we have to try to observe a pause between question and answer to allow the translation to catch up with us. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then let's begin. One thing that you touched on in direct examination but which was not entirely clear to me was with respect to this stills book that we've been dealing with relating to Srebrenica. What precisely was your role? I see throughout here there are a couple of persons that were identified by you, but what -- beyond that what specifically was your role in generating the Srebrenica stills booklet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the book instead of the video, it was at times selecting some of the photographs, also being part of capturing them, filling in the information as to the location, the source of the video that you see and the text, putting -- adding more to the table of contents, and checking some of that information as to the sites. And I also looked at the raw footage of almost every clip and just verified as well the identifications and that the -- the information that you see in terms of the text, the location, the source and all of that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now would you say that you are the person at the Office of the Prosecutor that was the most significantly involved in the creation of this particular Srebrenica stills booklet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's actually a difficult question in a way because the book was initially created prior to me. So the core of it existed before me and I have, along with several other people, added to it over the years. I'm certainly one of a number of substantial people, not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you in a position to identify for us what parts of this book were changed or modified that you added to the existing book that may have been used in other cases?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. Everything that came in certainly after -- well, let's put it -- anything that we as the OTP acquired footage-wise after 2002 is something that's been added. Certainly footage that's been received in -- since 2006 I would have played a role in in adding to the video and to the book, such as some of the Zepa footage, some of the footage that came in from the Mladic home search and seizure, the Milutinovic search and seizure, the Lesic footage that came in later, all of those have been added since the original trial video. And I think there's -- I'm sure there's more. If you want specifics we can go through the book, but off the top of my head those are examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that will suffice for now. Now at -- earlier today at temporary transcript page 28 you said that one of the attorneys played a substantial role in putting together this book. Could you identify for us who that was?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abeer Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did any other attorneys such as Mr. McCloskey or Mr. Groome or any of the other attorneys appearing in court for this case have any role in the creation or editing of this booklet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Peter would have -- McCloskey would have had certainly a role in terms of reviewing the book, deciding upon photographs to be kept in or kept out. So certainly he played a review and editing role.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And earlier in your testimony you talked about the identification of certain vehicles and work performed by the team prior to your arrival in generating this booklet. Am I correct that an individual named Mr. Richard Butler assisted in the creation of this booklet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that he had early on verified some of the vehicles, the Praga and the tank. That was his initial checking of the vehicle logs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was his role in the creation of this booklet limited to that or would it go beyond that aspect?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he played a large role. I think it was some of the investigators at that time working with Marta Fracassetti that worked more closely with her and that would have been Bruce Bursik, Jean Gagnon, and Dean Manning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can I take it from your answer that you did not, in fact, work with Mr. Butler in terms of your contribution to this booklet?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Rick Butler and I never overlapped in time here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now with regard to the identifications of both persons and locations in the still book, as I mentioned there are a few that identify -- that say they're identified by you by name. Can we take it from that that the ones that do not have a notation with your name are not the result of your personal identification of these persons and locations?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. Usually they'll be cited by somebody else. It doesn't mean that I can't identify them or have not been able to identify them, but that somebody else has -- prior to me had already done the identification and we've just kept it consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, throughout the video that was shown in court there was English subtitling and, first of all, the English subtitling that was apparent throughout would change at times where there was a black background. Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were additions or corrections that were made from the original subtitling, and -- so when a correction or something was changed, as everything was reviewed again, if there was a change then it was stamped -- that was put on top with a black background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I am looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One more question and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One more question and then we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who was responsible for putting the original English subtitling on the video or did it come to the OTP that way?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's -- the OTP did the original subtitling. I know that Zoran Lesic from our audio/visual production had done a lot of the subtitling. I don't know if he did the -- all of the original, but he's done the majority of it, I believe. I know it's -- I'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we're at a good point for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I have one small question. If you say he did the subtitling, do you mean in the technical way or that he did also listening to the audio and preparing the subtitles in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Thank you. That's a good point to clarify. It would have been with an interpreter initially who's done the transcript and the transcript -- and has done the entire transcript, sat down with Zoran Lesic, who is also a Serbian speaker, and together they have gone -- they have put in the subtitling. But technically he is doing it, but at times I know it's a joint -- it's a partnership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We will adjourn, but not until you have left the courtroom, Ms. Gallagher. We'd like to see you back next Tuesday at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn and we'll resume Tuesday, the 23rd of April, at -- in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of April, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
